newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan contractors' debt guarantees Y3 trln - Teikoku.
newsitem.headline: Japan contractors' debt guarantees Y3 trln - Teikoku.

text.p: The amount of debts guaranteed by 98 Japanese general contractors totalled 3.22 trillion yen at the end of September 1996, a survey by private research company Teikoku Databank Ltd showed on Tuesday.
The amount was down by only 3.4 percent, or 114.9 billion yen, from the end of March 1996, suggesting that the contractors failed to make progress in reducing debt guarantees, Teikoku Databank said.

Tobishima Corp held 666.7 billion yen worth of debt guarantees at the end of September, the largest among the firms. The figure was up 9.2 billion yen or 1.4 percent from the end-March level, it said.
Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd had the second largest amount of debt guarantees at 409 billion yen, followed by Aoki Corp at 296.3 billion yen and Hazama Corp at 216.7 billion yen, Teikoku Databank said.

The survey showed that 66 firms had cut the amount of their guarantees while 27 firms saw their figures rise during the half-year period to September. Taisei Corp was one such company that was able to substantially cut the amount of its debt guarantees.

During the 1980s "bubble era" of inflated asset and stock prices, general contractors actively guaranteed real estate companies" loans and loans of other firms that placed orders with them. After the bursting of the bubble, the loan guarantees became a drag on the financial health of contractors.
